prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Charlotte for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on the complexity of your case and what you value (experience, specialty training, technology, price, location, insurance acceptance, patient reviews). I can help you find the best match in Charlotte — here’s how to pick one and what to ask.

Who to look for
- Oral and maxillofacial surgeons or periodontists for placing implants (they receive surgical training).  
- Prosthodontists or implant-trained restorative dentists for the crown/prosthetic that goes on the implant. For complex cases it’s ideal to have both involved (surgeon + prosthodontist/restorative dentist).

Top credentials and signs of quality
- Board certification (American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery or American Board of Periodontology) or fellowship memberships.  
- Lots of implant cases (ask how many implants they place per year).  
- Use of cone-beam CT (CBCT) for planning and guided surgery.  
- Familiarity with major implant systems (Straumann, Nobel Biocare, Dentsply Sirona, Zimmer, etc.).  
- Good before/after photos of similar cases and patient testimonials.  
- Clear written treatment plan, timeline, and warranty/guarantee for work.  
- Good communication, clear fee estimate, and transparent complication policy.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants do you place per year? How many similar cases have you done?  
- Will you do the implant surgery and the restoration, or will other specialists be involved?  
- Do you use CBCT imaging and guided surgery?  
- What implant brand/system do you use and why?  
- What are the options for sedation/anesthesia?  
- What complications have you encountered and how were they handled?  
- What is the estimated total cost (surgery + implant + abutment + crown) and payment/financing options?  
- What is your follow-up schedule and implant success/failure rate?

Estimated costs & timeline (Charlotte, general range)
- Single implant (surgery + healing abutment) + crown: commonly $3,000–$6,000 total. Complex cases (bone grafts/sinus lifts/multiple implants) can be more.  
- Timeline: from 3–4 months (straightforward cases) to 6–12+ months if grafting/healing required.

How to find local candidates
- Use ADA Find-a-Dentist, AAOMS or AAP directories, Google Maps, Healthgrades, and Yelp.  
- Look for recent patient reviews, before/after photos, and clinic photos.  
- Ask your general dentist for a referral — they often coordinate care and know local specialists.

If you want, I can:
- Find top-rated implant specialists in Charlotte (tell me your ZIP or neighborhood and whether you have insurance).  
- Draft a short list of specific questions you can use at consultations.  

Which would you like me to do next?
